name: PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
mechanism: Clipped surrogate objective enabling stable multi-epoch policy-gradient updates
bottleneck_evidence: TRPO already framed reliable policy optimization as hard/complex; PPO simplifies it (arXiv:1502.05477, 2015)

name: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences (RLHF for LMs)
mechanism: Train reward model from preferences, fine-tune LM with RL+KL
target_problem: Reward for language hard to specify
bottleneck_evidence: Reward-from-preferences pioneered earlier to avoid hand-specified rewards (Christiano et al., arXiv:1706.03741, 2017)

name: Learning to summarize from human feedback
mechanism: Reward model on human comparisons, then RL-optimize summarizer
bottleneck_evidence: ROUGE's poor correlation with human judgment long documented (Better Summ. Eval. w/ Word Embeddings, arXiv:1508.06034, 2015)

name: WebGPT (best-of-N / rejection sampling)
mechanism: Behavior cloning plus reward-model best-of-N rejection sampling with browsing
bottleneck_evidence: Parametric LMs known to hallucinate facts; retrieval motivated to fix it (RAG, arXiv:2005.11401, 2020)

name: InstructGPT (RLHF / instruction following)
mechanism: SFT then reward model then PPO on human preference rankings
bottleneck_evidence: Misalignment of LM objective vs human intent already motivated reward learning (Ziegler et al., arXiv:1909.08593, 2019)

name: Constitutional AI (RLAIF for harmlessness)
mechanism: Self-critique/revision plus AI-feedback preference model for RL
bottleneck_evidence: Scalable oversight / costly human supervision flagged earlier (Scalable agent alignment via reward modeling, arXiv:1811.07871, 2018)

name: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
mechanism: Closed-form preference loss, no reward model or RL
bottleneck_evidence: InstructGPT's multi-stage reward-model+PPO pipeline already known complex/unstable (arXiv:2203.02155, 2022)

name: RLAIF (Scaling RLHF with AI Feedback)
mechanism: Off-the-shelf LLM labels preferences replacing human annotators
bottleneck_evidence: Cost of human harmlessness labels already motivated AI feedback (Constitutional AI, arXiv:2212.08073, 2022)

name: Transformer (Attention Is All You Need)
mechanism: Self-attention replaces recurrence/convolution for sequence modeling
bottleneck_evidence: RNN/LSTM sequential compute blocked parallelism and long-range deps (Hochreiter 1997; Bahdanau 1409.0473)

name: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts (Shazeer)
mechanism: Trainable gate sparsely routes tokens to expert subnetworks
bottleneck_evidence: Conditional computation to grow capacity cheaply was open problem (Bengio 1308.3432; Davis 1312.4461)

name: Switch Transformer
mechanism: Top-1 routing simplifies MoE to trillion parameters
bottleneck_evidence: Prior MoE suffered instability, communication, complexity costs (Shazeer 1701.06538; GShard Lepikhin 2006.16668)

name: Chinchilla scaling laws
mechanism: Scale model size and tokens equally for compute
bottleneck_evidence: Kaplan scaling laws over-prioritized size, leaving models undertrained (Kaplan 2001.08361)

name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
mechanism: Prompt exemplars elicit intermediate reasoning steps
bottleneck_evidence: LLMs known weak at arithmetic/multi-step reasoning despite scale (Brown GPT-3 2005.14165; Rae Gopher 2112.11446)

name: Self-Consistency
mechanism: Sample multiple reasoning paths, marginalize to majority answer
target_problem: Greedy CoT decoding picks suboptimal path
bottleneck_evidence: Refines CoT decoding; CoT itself only introduced ~2 months earlier (Wei 2201.11903)

name: Tree-of-Thoughts
mechanism: Search tree of thoughts with self-evaluation and backtracking
bottleneck_evidence: Critiques left-to-right CoT, a paradigm itself new in 2022 (Wei 2201.11903)

name: ReAct
mechanism: Interleave reasoning traces with tool/environment actions
bottleneck_evidence: Targets hallucination in just-introduced CoT, not long-standing recognized limitation (Wei 2201.11903)

name: Grokking
mechanism: Delayed generalization long after training-set overfitting
bottleneck_evidence: Reports a newly-discovered phenomenon rather than addressing a pre-existing widely-discussed bottleneck

name: Sparse Transformer
mechanism: Sparse factorizations of the attention matrix into O(n*sqrt(n)) patterns
target_problem: Quadratic attention cost on long sequences
bottleneck_evidence: Original Transformer states attention is O(n^2*d) per layer, costly for long n (arxiv 1706.03762)

name: Reformer
mechanism: Locality-sensitive hashing buckets queries/keys; reversible residual layers
bottleneck_evidence: Sparse Transformer already framed O(n^2) attention as prohibitive for long sequences (arxiv 1904.10509)

name: Longformer
mechanism: Sliding-window local attention plus task-motivated global attention
bottleneck_evidence: Sparse Transformer pre-dated it framing quadratic self-attention as the long-sequence limitation (arxiv 1904.10509)

name: Linformer
mechanism: Low-rank linear projection of keys/values to fixed dimension
bottleneck_evidence: Sparse Transformer (2019) framed O(n^2) attention as prohibitive for long sequences (arxiv 1904.10509)

name: Performer
mechanism: FAVOR+ positive orthogonal random features approximate softmax kernel linearly
bottleneck_evidence: Multiple prior works (Sparse Transformer 1904.10509, Reformer 2001.04451) framed quadratic attention as a known limitation

name: Nystromformer
mechanism: Nystrom method approximates softmax attention via landmark points
bottleneck_evidence: Efficient Transformers survey already cataloged quadratic attention as the core limitation (arxiv 2009.06732)

name: FNet
mechanism: Replaces self-attention with unparameterized 2D Fourier transform mixing
bottleneck_evidence: Efficient Transformers survey framed quadratic self-attention as the key efficiency bottleneck (arxiv 2009.06732)

name: Mamba
mechanism: Input-selective state space model with hardware-aware parallel scan
target_problem: Transformer quadratic scaling and slow inference
bottleneck_evidence: S4 already framed Transformer quadratic scaling on long sequences as a core limitation (arxiv 2111.00396)

name: Adapter Layers (Houlsby Adapters)
mechanism: Insert small trainable bottleneck MLPs between frozen transformer layers
target_problem: Full fine-tuning needs one model per task
bottleneck_evidence: This paper itself established the parameter-efficiency framing for transformers; no widely-cited pre-dating limitation paper found.

name: Prefix-Tuning
mechanism: Optimize continuous task-specific prefix vectors prepended to keys/values
target_problem: Storing full fine-tuned copy per task
bottleneck_evidence: GPT-3 framed per-task fine-tuning datasets/weight updates as a limitation. arXiv:2005.14165 (2020).

name: Prompt Tuning
mechanism: Learn soft prompt embeddings via backprop, freeze whole model
bottleneck_evidence: GPT-3 explicitly framed task-specific fine-tuning weight updates as a cost. arXiv:2005.14165 (2020).

name: LoRA
mechanism: Inject trainable low-rank matrices into frozen weights
bottleneck_evidence: Adapters add inference latency (Houlsby, arXiv:1902.00751, 2019); GPT-3 framed full-FT cost (arXiv:2005.14165, 2020).

name: BitFit
mechanism: Fine-tune only the bias terms, freeze all else
bottleneck_evidence: Adapters already framed full fine-tuning as parameter-inefficient needing per-task copies. arXiv:1902.00751 (2019).

name: Compacter
mechanism: Adapters via Kronecker-product shared slow plus rank-one fast weights
target_problem: Adapter parameter count still too high
bottleneck_evidence: Adapters established the parameter-count vs performance trade-off being minimized. arXiv:1902.00751 (2019).

name: (IA)^3
mechanism: Rescale key, value, and FFN activations by learned vectors
target_problem: In-context learning compute cost per inference
bottleneck_evidence: GPT-3 in-context learning reprocesses examples each call, a per-inference cost it critiqued. arXiv:2005.14165 (2020).

name: QLoRA
mechanism: LoRA over a frozen 4-bit NF4 quantized base model
target_problem: Memory cost of finetuning large LLMs
bottleneck_evidence: LoRA framed GPU memory of full fine-tuning as the limitation it reduced 3x. arXiv:2106.09685 (2021).

name: DoRA
mechanism: Decompose weights into magnitude and direction, LoRA on direction
target_problem: LoRA accuracy gap versus full fine-tuning
bottleneck_evidence: Gap was discussed informally, but no clear pre-dating (before Feb 2024) arxiv paper framing it as a widely-discussed limitation; 'LoRA Learns Less' (arXiv:2405.09673) post-dates DoRA.

name: Batch Normalization
mechanism: Normalize layer activations per mini-batch with learned scale/shift
bottleneck_evidence: Deep nets needed low LRs and careful init; covariate shift known (Shimodaira 2000)

name: Adam
mechanism: Per-parameter adaptive LR from first/second gradient moment estimates
bottleneck_evidence: Adaptive LR an active problem; AdaGrad (Duchi 2011) and RMSProp (Tieleman/Hinton 2012) predate

name: Dropout
mechanism: Randomly drop units during training to prevent co-adaptation
bottleneck_evidence: Overfitting was the canonical known problem; dropout's own 2012 preprint (arXiv:1207.0580) predates JMLR version

name: Layer Normalization
mechanism: Normalize across features per sample, independent of batch
bottleneck_evidence: BatchNorm's batch-size dependence and RNN difficulty explicitly noted in Ioffe & Szegedy 2015

name: Label Smoothing
mechanism: Replace hard one-hot targets with softened label distribution
bottleneck_evidence: Inception-v3 introduced it; overconfidence not a widely-discussed named bottleneck before this paper

name: Mixup
mechanism: Train on convex combinations of input/label pairs
bottleneck_evidence: ERM memorization of random labels documented (Zhang et al. 2017, arXiv:1611.03530)

name: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM)
mechanism: Minimize worst-case loss in a parameter neighborhood (flat minima)
bottleneck_evidence: Flat-vs-sharp minima generalization widely studied (Keskar et al. 2016, arXiv:1609.04836; Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997)

name: SGDR / Cosine LR Schedule
mechanism: Cosine-anneal learning rate with periodic warm restarts
bottleneck_evidence: LR schedule sensitivity long known; step/exponential decay standard but ad hoc (Bengio 2012 practical recommendations)

name: Gradient Clipping (norm clipping)
mechanism: Rescale gradient when its norm exceeds a threshold
bottleneck_evidence: Exploding/vanishing gradients the canonical RNN problem (Bengio et al. 1994; Hochreiter 1991 thesis)
